To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a herpesvirus expressing a constitutvely active form of heat shock transcription factor (HSF) protects neuronal cells against thermal and ischaemic stress.

(1) a constitutively activated form of heat shock transcription factor (HSF1), which is not stress‐inducible, is able to induce the expression of a restricted range of heat shock proteins (hsp) in neurons and (2) this virus vector protects neurons against subsequent thermal or hypoxic–ischaemic stress but does not protect them against apoptosis.

(i) the constitutively active HSF1 mutant is expressed at high levels in neurons, (ii) it induces HSP70 but not HSP27, (iii) it protects neurons against thermal or ischaemia stress but not against apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the manipulation of HSP gene expression in order to improve neuronal cell survival in the face of stressful stimuli.
the manipulation of the heat shock response in mammalian cells.
the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSF1 is a useful target for the development of gene therapy for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.
the HSF vector is useful for protecting cells against thermal or ischaemia but not against apoptosis.
the virus vector is a useful and powerful means of delivering a constitutively activated HSF1 into cells, which in turn induces a protective response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the constitutively active HSF1 is able to induce the expression of a subset of HSPs in neuronal cells and that this subset is sufficient to protect these cells from thermal and ischaemic stress, but is insufficient to protect from apoptosis.
the virus vector expressing the constitutively active HSF1 protected neuronal cells from stress‐induced injury but not from apoptosis.
the virus vector is a useful tool for studying HSF and HSP function but it is not a general panacea for the induction of HSPs and protection against stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the constitutively active HSF1 mutant is able to protect neurons against heat and ischemic stress but not against apoptosis.
constitutively active heat shock factor (HSF1‐Δ) is not sufficient to protect cells from apoptosis.
constitutive expression of HSF1 in neurons protects them from heat shock and ischaemia, but not from apoptosis.
